title: ODA as a share of gross national income, by DAC donor
description: Each bar is one donor's official development assistance divided by its gross national income.
content:
The dotted line marks the UN target of 0.7%.
- Hover over a bar to see the donor's value.
- Select a year to compare donors in that year.

title: Norway gives the most aid as a share of income
description: ODA as a share of gross national income for each DAC member.
content: Values come from the OECD's DAC1 table. Norway, Luxembourg and Sweden are above the 0.7% target.

title: Debt service by creditor type
description: Principal and interest paid on external public debt, split into bilateral, multilateral and private creditors.
content:
Each column is one year. The segments add up to total debt service.
Amounts are in current US dollars.

title: Debt service of low-income countries
description: Debt service has more than doubled since 2012. Payments to private creditors make up the fastest-growing part.

title: Climate finance from developed countries
description: Climate finance provided and mobilised, as reported to the OECD, by type of finance.
content:
Total climate finance reached USD 115.9 billion in 2022.
- Public bilateral: 41.0
- Multilateral: 50.6
- Private mobilised: 21.9

title: Climate finance by purpose
description: Mitigation, adaptation and cross-cutting finance, as donors report it.
content: Donors mark each project as mitigation, adaptation or both. A project that serves both appears as cross-cutting, so the three parts do not overlap.

title: Total ODA in 2023
description: The key number is total net ODA from DAC members in the year shown, in current US dollars.
content:
Net ODA from DAC members, in current US dollars:
$223,300,000,000

title: Total ODA
description: This key number follows the latest year the OECD reports, so it changes when new figures are published.
content: Net ODA counts grants in full and loans at their grant equivalent, so repayments are not subtracted.

title: Top recipients of bilateral ODA
description: The table lists recipients by the bilateral ODA they received, largest first.
content:
Ukraine heads the list, ahead of Türkiye and Ethiopia.
Regional and unspecified amounts are left out of the ranking.

title: Bilateral ODA by recipient
description: A table of bilateral ODA by recipient country, which you can sort by any column.
content:
- Recipient: the country that received the aid.
- Gross disbursements: what donors paid out in the year.
- Share: the recipient's share of all bilateral ODA.

title: Snapshot: ODA to sub-Saharan Africa
description: This snapshot keeps the data as it stood when it was published.
content: In this snapshot, sub-Saharan Africa received about a third of bilateral ODA. The share has fallen since 2010.

title: ODA to sub-Saharan Africa over time
description: A line for each year's share of bilateral ODA that went to sub-Saharan Africa.
content: The line follows the latest data from the source. A dashed segment marks preliminary figures, which the source revises.

title: The UK has cut aid to 0.5% of national income
description: UK ODA as a share of gross national income, with the 0.7% target.
content: The target line is the UN's 0.7% of gross national income.

title: UK ODA as a share of national income
description: The United Kingdom's ODA divided by its gross national income, year by year.
content: The UK wrote the 0.7% target into law in 2015. The International Development Act sets out when the government may fall short of it.

title: Interest paid on external debt
description: Interest payments are at a record high. This chart shows interest on long-term external debt.
content: Figures come from the World Bank's International Debt Statistics.

title: Interest paid on external debt, by income group
description: Interest on long-term external debt for low-income and lower-middle-income countries.
content: The World Bank's International Debt Statistics records each loan a country reports, so the totals cover public and publicly guaranteed debt.

title: Health ODA
description: ODA to the health sector, by donor.
content:
- The United States gives the most.
- Health aid rose 12% in 2021.
- Amounts are in constant 2022 dollars.

title: Health ODA by donor
description: ODA to the health sector, by donor, in constant 2022 US dollars.
content:
- Each bar is one donor.
- Select a sector above the chart to switch from health.
- Constant dollars remove the effect of inflation, so years compare by volume.

title: Countries in debt distress
description: Countries the IMF and World Bank rate as in debt distress or at high risk of it.
content: As of 2024, 34 countries are in distress or at high risk. Ratings come from the joint debt sustainability framework for low-income countries.

title: Debt distress ratings
description: The IMF and World Bank rating of each low-income country's risk of debt distress.
content:
- Low: the country can meet its debts under most shocks.
- Moderate: it can meet them unless a large shock hits.
- High: it is likely to struggle to meet them.
- In distress: it already cannot meet them without restructuring.

title: Private finance mobilised
description: Private money that official finance brings into projects, as donors report it.
content: This chart follows the source, so its values change when the OECD publishes new figures. Mobilised private finance remains below USD 20 billion a year.

title: Private finance mobilised by instrument
description: Private finance mobilised by guarantees, syndicated loans, credit lines and direct investment.
content: The OECD counts private finance as mobilised when an official intervention causes it. Each instrument has its own counting rule, so totals are not comparable with flows of other kinds.

title: Humanitarian aid
description: Humanitarian ODA by donor.
content:
Humanitarian aid accounts for one in every seven dollars of ODA.
Germany and the United States give over half of it.

title: Humanitarian aid, by donor
description: Humanitarian ODA from each DAC member, in current US dollars.
content: Humanitarian aid covers emergency response, reconstruction and disaster prevention. It does not include development projects in the same countries.

title: The 0.7% target
description: Which donors meet the UN target for ODA as a share of gross national income.
content:
Only five donors met the target in 2023:
- Norway
- Luxembourg
- Sweden
- Germany
- Denmark

title: The 0.7% target and who meets it
description: Each donor's ODA as a share of gross national income, against the UN target.
content: A donor above the line meets the target in the year selected. Move the year slider to see other years.

title: Net flows on debt to Africa
description: Net flows are new loans disbursed minus principal repaid.
content: Net flows to Africa turned negative in 2023. A negative value means a country repaid more than it borrowed.

title: Net flows on external debt
description: New disbursements minus principal repayments, by region.
content: Bars above zero mean a region borrowed more than it repaid. Bars below zero mean it repaid more.

title: Education ODA, 2015 to 2023
description: ODA to education by year, in constant dollars.
content: Education aid has stagnated since 2019, at about USD 16 billion a year. Basic education gets less than a third.

title: Education ODA by level
description: ODA to education, split into basic, secondary and post-secondary.
content: Basic education covers primary schooling and early childhood. Post-secondary includes scholarships and imputed student costs, which some donors count in their own country.
